C-reactive protein (CRP) is a protein made by the liver. CRP levels in the blood increase when there is a conditioncausing inflammation somewhere in the body. A CRP test measures the amount of CRP in the blood to detect inflammation due to acuteconditions or to monitor the severity of disease in chronic conditions.

Serological test for Tb Diagnosis

Commercial serological tests may provide inconsistent and imprecise estimates of sensitivity and specificity. There is no evidence that existing commercial serological assays improve patient important outcomes. WHO Expert Group strongly recommended that these tests not be used for the diagnosis of pulmonary and extra-pulmonary TB.

Recent Advances

For many years, there was only one way to test for TB: the tuberculin skin test (TST). This is no longer the case, as there are now two categories of tests to detect TB infection: the TST and interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs), including the T-SPOT.TB test and QuantiFERON®-TB Gold Plus test (QFT®-Plus).All of these tests are used as diagnostic aids in determining the presence of latent or active TB, these tests are available at Makhdoom Labs.

T-SPOT.TB test

The T-SPOT.TB testis a unique, single visit blood test for tuberculosis designed to reduce assay variability and maximize sensitivity, even in the immunocompromised.

False Negativity of Zn Smear Microscopy

Zn smear microscopy has some limitations, like the **Low sensitivity (22-43%)** and **High false negativity (19-29%)** The threshold of this technique for detection of AFB is **104 to 105 bacilli/ml** to givepositive AFB smear. Therefore, cases at initial stages of TB and heaving very low AFB load can be falsely reported as negative.

Gold Standard for TB Diagnosis

Lowenstein Jensen (LJ)culture for MTB remains superior to ZN smear microscopy as it can detect MTB as low as 10 to 100 viable bacteria/ml, but this conventional culture technique leads to considerable delay in Tb diagnosis.

WHO Recommendations

WHO recommended GeneXpert (rapid PCR-based technique) as a screening marker for the diagnosis of pulmonary & extra-pulmonary TB .

METHODOLOGY: Real - Time PCR (Rotor Gene - Q®, 5 Plex by QIAGEN GmbH)

PROCEDURE:

 

Geno Sen’s HCV Genotyping (RG) Real Time PCR kit was used.

This procedure involved extraction of hepatitis C RNA from 140 µl of serum from the patient’s sample that based on reverse transcription of the target RNA to generate complementary DNA (cDNA), followed by amplification of target DNA which is then hybridized to oligonucleotide probes specific to each HCV genotype. Finally the probe bound amplified product is simultaneously detected by Real Time PCR technology.

 

COMMENTS:

Presently HCV can be divided into at least 6 major genotypes and a series of sub-types. There is increasing evidence that patient infected with different HCV genotypes may have different clinical profiles, severity of liver disease and response to alpha interferon therapy. Patients with type 2 and 3 (3a & 3b) HCV infection are more likely to have a sustained response to therapy than patients with type 1 (1a & 1b). Therefore the patient genotype should be taken into consideration when considering interferon therapy (Dusheiko et al., 1996; B. M. J., 312:)

 

Sometime an Untypable genotype result occurs due to following mentioned reasons:

 

1. The patent is negative for HCV RNA even though ELISA positive (No active infection)

2. The Titer of HCV RNA is below the sensitivity limit of genotyping assay (< 33.6 IU/ml)

3. The patient has received standard Interferon + Ribavirin therapy in near past, even though with high HCV RNA load and LFTs levels at the time of sample collection. Because Untypable genotypes are more common in previously treated and replaced patients; as the drug pressure cause mutation in HCV RNA, resulting in the emergence of new mutated quasi - species that cannot be genotyped by the available genotyping assays.

Methodology:

1. Low titers of auto-antibodies may occur in healthy patients. For this reason, low positive results (close to the CO, between 8 and 10 U/ml), although valid, should be considered equivocal. In such cases, the retesting of the patient, preferably by using a new sample, is recommended. If the result remains equivocal on retesting, other diagnostic tests and/ or clinical information should be used to help determine the autoimmune status of the patient.


2. Sequential sampling (at different dates) of an autoimmune patient can sometimes lead to different results from one sample to another. This difference can have several reasons: the patient`s treatment, the evolution of the disease, or a seroconversion. In the specific case of seroconversion, the result can be positive for an auto-antibody in an early sampling of the patient., and become positive for another auto antibody in a later sampling of the same patient.

Note:ADA is an enzyme that is widely distributed in human tissues, including T lymphocytes. Elevated serum ADA activity has been observed in patients with acute hepatitis, alcoholic hepatic fibrosis, chronic active hepatitis, liver cirrhosis, viral hepatitis and hepatoma. Increased ADA activity is also observed in patients with tuberculous effusions. Determination of ADA in patient serum may aid in the diagnosis of liver diseases in combination with ALT or Gamma GT tests. ADA assay may also be useful in the diagnostics of tuberculous pleuritis.

fixremarks:
A Negative QFT result means that patient is not suffering from Mycobacterium tuberculosis. False negative results may be due to different stages of infection and affected immune response.


Positive QFT result should not be considered as definitive diagnosis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It may be due to other bacterial/viral infection response. It is suggested to correlate with clinical condition of the patient.
